text:
Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a central repository. A key part of CI is the use of automated builds, which compile the code every time a change is made. After the build, the system automatically runs tests to check that the new code does not break existing features.

These CI pipelines help catch issues early, often within minutes of a change. Instead of discovering problems days later, developers receive immediate feedback. This saves time and reduces stress, as small problems are fixed quickly before they become major issues. Overall, CI makes software development faster, safer, and more collaborative.
